answer: Steel nets hang below the cliff to catch falling rock, and the inspectors count and clear the stones every month, recording each net's own load. A marble net hung by an unlicensed hand fails the record: at the pearl of the net the anchors must match the cliff's own bolts, and a strange net sags at the first frost. Forging the record means hiring an inspection crew for a season, buying steel and paying 14,200, while the meadow entry in the inspection book is read at every climb, so a net whose stones were never counted is taken down.
